findings.evidence: File header: `variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`. The proof uses `hasDerivWithinAt_iff_tendsto_slope'`, `mem_tangentConeAt_of_frequently` and `slope_def_module`, none of which involve the inner product.
findings.fix: Give it its own binder `{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]`, either by declaring it before the inner-product `variable` or in a section with a normed-space `variable`.
findings.issue: `HasDerivWithinAt.mem_posTangentConeAt` requires `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`, inherited from the file-level `variable`. Its statement and proof only use `HasDerivWithinAt`, `slope` and `tangentConeAt`, so `[NormedSpace ℝ E]` is enough. Without the change it cannot be used in Banach spaces or for non-Hilbert norms.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/ODE/PicardLindelof.lean:717 has `variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]` for the existence section, and `of_contDiffAt_one [NormedSpace ℝ E]` is at line 676.
findings.fix: State it with `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]`.
findings.issue: `LocallyLipschitz.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt` (Picard–Lindelöf existence) also inherits `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`. It only needs a complete normed space, which is the setting of the Mathlib results it uses (`IsPicardLindelof.of_time_independent` and `exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt₀`).

summary: Two declarations that never use the inner product still require `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`, because they pick it up from the file-level `variable` line. The convex-invariance statements are at the natural level.
